newsitem.title: INDIA: India rains on course wait for July El Nino update.
newsitem.headline: India rains on course wait for July El Nino update.

text.p: The impact of the developing El Nino global weather pattern on India's monsoon will not become clear until late July, but the June-September rains are now on course, the Indian Meteorological Department said on Friday.
"If by the end of July we don't get rains as expected, only then can we say that the El Nino factor is affecting rains in the country," IMD director S.C.Goel told Reuters.
"But as of now, there is nothing to worry about. Right now the progress of monsoon rains is satisfactory."

Goel said his department had taken note of the El Nino effect while making its monsoon forecast in May and had predicted that rainfall would be on the negative side of the long-term average (92 percent).
El Nino raises the water temperature off the coast of South America and can disrupt weather patterns worldwide, creating drought conditions in some areas.
The phenomenon and its opposite, La Nina (Australia wet/California dry), will be one of the major themes at a world weather conference beginning in Melbourne on Tuesday.
Goel said the El Nino factor had been unfavourable in some previous years but had not affected India's annual monsoon.
"Therefore it is possible that El Nino may not affect Indian monsoon rains at all," he said.
But U.S. meteorologists have said the current El Nino is the strongest developing pattern since 1983, a year of severe drought and also flooding in many Asian countries.

Goel said the IMD had advised the Indian Agriculture Ministry to take precautions in case there were problems with the monsoon, which is critical for the country's economy because of its huge agricultural sector.
"There is no harm in making any contingency plans," he said.
